topic: Bayes' Theorem: The Geometry of Changing Your Mind
target_audience: University students or advanced high school students with a basic grasp of probability

sections.title: The Core Intuition: Probability as Space
sections.content: Introduce the prerequisite concept: Probability is not just a number, but an 'area' within a total space of possibilities. We represent the entire world of possibilities as a 1x1 square (Area = 1).
sections.example: Imagine a 10x10 grid representing a forest. If 10% of the forest contains Rare Blue butterflies, we color 10% of the square's area blue. This is our 'Prior' belief before seeing any evidence.

sections.title: The Scenario: Prior Probabilities
sections.content: Establish a base rate (Prior) using a character-driven example. Split the square vertically into two rectangles based on the initial probability of two competing hypotheses.
sections.example: A robot detective is looking for a 'Glitch-Bot'. In a factory, 20% are Glitch-Bots (Small Rectangle) and 80% are Normal-Bots (Large Rectangle). Visually, the square is now split 2:8.

sections.title: The Evidence: Conditional Likelihood
sections.content: Introduce new evidence that has different 'hit rates' for each hypothesis. Graphically, we slice the horizontal axis of our existing rectangles. This creates sub-areas representing 'True Positives' and 'False Positives'.
sections.example: The detective uses a 'Spark Test'. 90% of Glitch-Bots spark, but 10% of Normal-Bots also spark by accident. We shade the top 90% of the Glitch-Bot rectangle and the top 10% of the Normal-Bot rectangle.

sections.title: The Geometric Update: Slicing the Universe
sections.content: When evidence occurs (the 'Spark' happens), the 'non-sparking' areas of our square vanish. They are no longer possible. Our 'universe' of possibilities shrinks to only the shaded areas.
sections.example: The robot sparks! We visually discard the bottom (non-sparking) parts of the square. We are left with a thin slice from the Normal-Bots and a tall slice from the Glitch-Bots.

sections.title: The Posterior: Re-normalizing the World
sections.content: The final step of Bayes' Theorem: Re-stretching the remaining area to fill a 1x1 square again. The 'Posterior' probability is the ratio of the 'True Evidence' area to the 'Total Evidence' area.
sections.example: We compare the area of (Glitch-Bots who spark) against the total area of (All bots who spark). Even though the test is 90% accurate, because Normal-Bots were so common, the resulting 'New Area' for Glitch-Bots might only be 69%.

sections.title: From Geometry to Formula
sections.content: Translate the visual stretching and slicing into the algebraic form of Bayes' Theorem, showing how each term corresponds to a geometric transformation.
sections.example: P(H|E) = [P(E|H) * P(H)] / P(E). We show that the numerator is the 'True Positive' area and the denominator is the 'Total Shaded' area.
